boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus settings for collaborative work, quiet reading, informal meetups, and outdoor study, documented by USD’s library and university-center pages.

cards.title: Copley Ground Floor Exchange
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · collaborative study level
cards.notes: Bring a project partner or small group and use the ground-floor setting for active learning and conversation at low to moderate volume.
cards.short_summary: A library level designated for collaborative work and extended conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies Copley’s lower level as the Ground Floor Exchange, intended for collaborative work and extended conversations.
cards.access_notes: Library space; follow current library access rules and the published quiet policy.

cards.title: Copley Lounge
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · lower level
cards.notes: Use this lounge when your group needs to compare notes or continue a conversation without moving into the library’s quiet-study areas.
cards.short_summary: A designated lounge where collaboration and extended conversation are allowed.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s library policy allows extended conversations and collaboration in Copley Lounge.
cards.access_notes: Library space; keep conversation within the library’s stated noise expectations.

cards.title: Copley’s group-room network
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · reservable group spaces
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a shared work session, then check in on arrival; these rooms are intended for students working and studying together.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms designed specifically for group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: USD states that Copley group study rooms are a community resource for students to work and study together, and current USD students may reserve them.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is limited to current USD students; group rooms are not for individual study or socializing.

cards.title: Mother Hill Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · absolute quiet study
cards.notes: Choose this reading room for solo, silent concentration; plan calls and group discussion for another campus setting before you enter.
cards.short_summary: A named Copley reading room reserved for absolute quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: USD’s quiet policy reserves the Mother Hill Reading Room for absolute quiet study and prohibits talking there.
cards.access_notes: No talking is permitted; observe current Copley Library access rules.

cards.title: Garden Study Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · second-floor Scholarly Living Room
cards.notes: Settle in here for quiet academic work, and save longer conversations for the library’s collaborative spaces on the ground floor.
cards.short_summary: A named room within Copley’s second-floor quiet-study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: USD includes the Garden Study Room in Copley’s second-floor Scholarly Living Room, which is intended for quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Extended conversations and loud talking are not appropriate in this second-floor quiet-study area.

cards.title: Journals Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · second-floor reading space
cards.notes: Use this room for focused reading of academic journals or magazines, keeping the space quiet for others working nearby.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room in Copley’s quiet second-floor study area.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists the Journals Reading Room within Copley’s second-floor Scholarly Living Room, intended for quiet academic learning.
cards.access_notes: Not available for reservation or class and organizational meetings, per USD’s room policy.

cards.title: Camino Stacks study spaces
cards.subtitle: Copley Library · ground-floor study seating
cards.notes: Use the study seating in the Camino Stacks when you need a ground-floor work spot where moderate conversation is permitted.
cards.short_summary: Named study spaces among Copley’s Camino Hall stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: USD lists study spaces in the Camino Stacks and includes Camino Stacks among ground-floor areas where online meetings are allowed.
cards.access_notes: Located in Copley Library; follow its current access and noise policies.

cards.title: Mother Teresa Plaza
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · informal study and gathering
cards.notes: Meet a friend, spread out for a study break, or use the grass for an informal group session while respecting scheduled reservations.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor plaza used for studying, dining, rallies, and informal gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes Mother Teresa Plaza as a gathering place where students study, dine, hold rallies, meet friends, or relax on the grass.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: Informal use is subject to reservations through USD’s event-registration system.

cards.title: SLP 3rd Floor Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · shaded outdoor seating
cards.notes: Take a laptop or lunch outside under the market umbrellas, then check the reservation schedule if you plan to use the courtyard later in the day.
cards.short_summary: A shaded Student Life Pavilion courtyard for informal lunches and study.
cards.evidence_claim: USD describes the SLP 3rd Floor Courtyard as a place to meet for lunch or study, with stated informal-use and reservation periods.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: USD lists informal use weekdays 8 a.m.–5 p.m. and weekends 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; reservations may take priority at other times.

cards.title: Frank Warren Lounge and Patio
cards.subtitle: Student Life Pavilion · open-use patio
cards.notes: Use the patio for a relaxed catch-up or a short outdoor reset; ask University Center Operations or Frank’s Lounge staff before using fire pits.
cards.short_summary: An open-use patio designed for relaxing and catching up with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: USD identifies the patio in front of Frank’s Lounge as an open-use area for relaxing and catching up with friends, with staff assistance for fire pits.
cards.source_title: Dine, Shop, Meet — Hahn University Center and Student Life Pavilion
cards.access_notes: Open-use patio; consult University Center Operations or Frank’s Lounge staff for fire-pit assistance.
